history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V18 scored workload, mode, job count, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability ruling, acceptance decision, attribution metric, external-suite boundary, and publication boundary. It adds a separate zig-js-only cold Context lifecycle evidence profile; that profile is not a scored representative family and does not enter any cross-engine or aggregate result. Any later workload, Context option, boundary, checksum, telemetry field, retention policy, runner, integration ruling, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds a frozen, non-scored cold Context lifecycle profile and teaches the exact-parent collector to preserve its phase, RSS, soak, and finalizer telemetry without changing any inherited representative row.

contract_changes: frontend compiler counters are retained with every sample
competing long-running jobs reject collection before sampling
transient overlap rejects the affected exact pair
structural self-test JSON fixtures are cloned without a host convenience global
context_lifecycle samples preserve and validate their frozen auxiliary telemetry row
exact_parent_integration.publication_boundary: Only an explicitly selected quiet-reference host on AC power may support an efficiency or lifecycle claim. Required counters must be measured and stable at at most 5% RSD, every thermal observation must remain nominal, generated-code/cache claims additionally require their exact category metric, and every raw sample remains visible. Context lifecycle collection additionally requires the frozen options/checksum profile, exact phase and finalizer reconciliation, and bounded post-destroy RSS checkpoints. Diagnostic hosts never gate or support a public ratio.

context_lifecycle_integration.publication_boundary: This is a zig-js-only causal evidence profile, never a JavaScriptCore ratio or representative aggregate. A speed or retention claim requires a dated exact-parent raw artifact from the declared quiet macOS reference host; structural fixtures and diagnostic local runs establish only schema and runner correctness.
